title: Explainable gradient boosting predicts persistent sepsis-associated acute kidney injury
summary: A gradient boosting machine with 12 features, chosen among eight algorithms, predicted persistent sepsis-associated AKI with internal AUC 0.870 and external AUC 0.891 (MIMIC-III), 0.932 (eICU) and 0.983 (hospital retrospective cohort). In a prospective ICU cohort it reached AUC 0.852 against 0.821 for urinary CCL14. Prospective data came from a single ICU, the prospective cohort size is not in the abstract, and the 0.983 result comes from a retrospective hospital cohort.
ai_technology: Gradient boosting machine (12 features, selected among 8 machine-learning algorithms) predicting persistent sepsis-associated AKI
organization: Northern Jiangsu People's Hospital, Yangzhou University

evidence.tested: External validation in MIMIC-III, eICU and hospital retrospective cohorts, and a prospective ICU cohort compared with urinary CCL14.
evidence.unknown: Prospective cohort size and multi-site prospective performance; clinical benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient boosting model predicted persistent AKI from routine clinical features.
